attestation: HSH Intelligence — coverage and precision attestation
what_this_is: The statements a SAMPLE CANNOT ESTABLISH, published separately and signed with the same key that signs TRUST-ROOTS.json. A subset proves nothing about its superset, so coverage, denominators and precision are attested here rather than implied by a sample.
what_the_interval_does_not_cover: The intervals above are Wilson bounds on sampling error, given the denominator. Two things they do not describe. FIRST, records the verifier could not decide are excluded from the denominator rather than counted against it, so precision is measured over the records this instrument could read — the `sampled`, `confirmed`, `contradicted` and `inconclusive` counts are all published so you can recompute it either way. SECOND, an interval assumes the draw is fixed. Ours is: the sample is drawn deterministically and three consecutive runs of the instrument produced byte-identical verdicts on every stratum and every drawn record. Before 2026-09-17 that was not true, and figures published earlier are historical readings that cannot be re-derived.

how_to_read_this.claim_type: `sampled` carries a confidence interval and generalises within the declared frame. `census` means every member was examined: there is no sampling risk and NO interval is quoted, because quoting one would imply an inference that was not made. They are not interchangeable.
how_to_read_this.frame_coverage_pct: The share of the stratum's population the verifier could actually reach and read. Precision is measured within that frame, and a figure outside it is not claimed.
how_to_read_this.verdict: SHIP means the stratum met its floor and its links are published as established. HOLD means it did not: those links are NOT shipped as linked, and the rows carry a named reason instead.
